item: Protected mode names the app only in its own Wikipedia, Wikidata and dump requests to Wikimedia; two operator probes that bypassed the proxy now follow the mode (R657)
summary: R657, ruled on item 68's read. BEFORE: the Settings note, the user manual, docs/SECURITY.md and the settings endpoint's note said protected mode sends a generic User-Agent. The collector did (make_fetcher); a guarded session did not: _session_for set the caller's own agent before it read the mode, so every API client built on guarded_session (the statistics fetchers, OSM downloads and replication, self-update, the model installer, topic discovery, IPCC, the Wikidata and Wikipedia clients) named the app through the proxy. Worse, found by both security reads: a field check (host_reach) and the release run's law probe built EthicalFetcher by hand, so in protected mode they went out with NO proxy (and local DNS) and the bot's name. NOW: in protected mode a guarded session sends GENERIC_USER_AGENT to every host except the Wikimedia hosts the app's own Wikipedia, Wikidata and dump clients are confined to, whose User-Agent policy asks API clients to name themselves; those keep the caller's descriptive agent and still go through the proxy. The list is one constant, DESCRIPTIVE_AGENT_HOSTS: .wikipedia.org (every edition, not the portal), www.wikidata.org, query.wikidata.org, wikimedia.org (pageviews), dumps.wikimedia.org, stream.wikimedia.org, ores.wikimedia.org; a test holds it equal to those clients' own host lists, so no other or third-party-hosted Wikimedia name is on it. keeps_descriptive_agent reads the URL both ways requests and urllib3 read it, and both readings must be https to a listed host, else the generic agent (plain http would carry the name past the exit in clear text). The choice is made in GuardedSession.send, which requests calls for the first request and for every redirect hop, so a hop from Wikimedia to another host gets the generic agent and a User-Agent a request carried itself is replaced. Transparent mode is unchanged. The two probes take make_fetcher (proxy and generic agent in protected mode; with no proxy, refused by name and recorded as their result), and a test fails on any module but src/safety/fetcher.py and the soak harness that builds an EthicalFetcher itself. TEXTS: the Settings note says protected mode routes the app's web fetches through your proxy with a generic User-Agent, except in its API and dump requests to Wikimedia's servers, which still name the tool because Wikimedia's API policy asks for it (an article collected from Wikipedia gets the generic agent), and that the newsletter mailbox pull, OpenTimestamps anchoring and the local-AI downloads connect directly (they did before; the consent popup's hover already said so per lane, the note said every fetch); the warning beside it no longer sends SOCKS users to an optional [safety] extra that does not exist (PySocks is core since R656) and says SOCKS proxies such as Tor need nothing extra installed; both keyed in all 12 locales (Hindi and Chinese now use one word for protected). The option label (Protected, generic UA + proxy) is unchanged: the note directly above it states the exception. docs/USER_MANUAL.md (both places it describes protected mode), docs/SECURITY.md (the hosts, the constant, the redirect, https and collector rules, the two probes, the direct lanes), the endpoint's note, the settings module docstring, the guarded_session docstring, docs/GOVERNANCE.md and docs/product/USE_CASES.md say the same. TESTS: tests/test_protected_user_agent_r657.py, 46 tests: the list equals the clients' hosts; eight Wikimedia URLs keep the agent; other hosts, lookalikes, Wikimedia names off the list, the bare domains, plain http and loopback get the generic one, as do unreadable URLs and both directions of a parser split; a real protected-mode session through a recording adapter sends the generic agent except to Wikimedia, replaces an agent the request carried, gives each redirect hop the agent its own host is owed, and a following session does the same; transparent mode names the app everywhere as before; both probes fetch through the proxy with the generic agent, and with no proxy are refused before any fetch; the construction ratchet; the note and the warning in index.html and in all 12 locales, the old keys gone, and each text states the exception. tests/test_settings_read_fails_closed.py: a held session built on unreadable settings (read as protected) carries the generic agent and keeps its own. Against the base, 45 of 46 fail (the one that passes pins transparent mode). Mutants: 14, all killed (one parser reading only, either way; no https check; a .wikimedia.org suffix; a loose suffix match; always or never descriptive; no protected_agent; no session-level generic header; setdefault for the override; no trailing-dot strip; either probe by hand; any reading instead of both). Two independent security reads of the first build (NO-GO and GO-with-must-fix, both naming the probes) folded; a fresh read of the fold: GO, no must-fix (it grepped src/ for every HTTP client and found no other path that names the app or skips the proxy beyond the stated direct lanes; it fed the real Wikimedia URL builders through the check, all kept; 9 more mutants caught); its should-fixes folded (the direct lanes named in the note, the API-and-dump wording, the refusal test names TransportUnavailable). NOT CHANGED, stated: the collector already sent the generic agent; a host that refuses a browser-like agent now refuses protected-mode requests (none the app calls is known to); separate circuits still do not make Wikidata lookups unlinkable (68(b)); the newsletter mailbox pull, OpenTimestamps (the library's own client and agent) and the local-AI downloads still connect directly in protected mode (pre-existing, each behind its own consent; now said in the note); make_fetcher(**overrides) would accept a proxy=None or user_agent override (no caller passes one); a future Wikimedia client on a host the list lacks would get the generic agent until its host is added. Release-notes line: «In protected mode the app no longer names itself to the sites it downloads data from, and two diagnostic checks that went around your proxy now use it: only the app's Wikipedia, Wikidata and dump requests, which Wikimedia asks to be named, still carry its name.»
